13. The Positive Theory of Equilibrium

Does equilibrium exist, is it unique, can we get there — answered through the geometry of excess demand and tatonnement dynamics.

  • Tatonnement Dynamics — The auctioneer raises and lowers the price watching excess demand: pt+1=pt+k z(pt)p_{t+1} = p_t + k\, z(p_t)pt+1​=pt​+kz(pt​). Raising the speed kkk quickens convergence — until past a threshold it diverges instead. An overeager auctioneer destabilizes the market.
  • Excess Demand: Existence and Uniqueness — Where the excess demand curve z1(p1)z_1(p_1)z1​(p1​) crosses zero is equilibrium. In the Cobb-Douglas economy there is always exactly one (gross substitutes), and Walras' law p⋅z=0p \cdot z = 0p⋅z=0 holds. Switch to illustrative mode and there can be three equilibria — uniqueness is not free.
